name: Clay pink
lede: Clay pink is a greyish, reddish orange named for the color of clay earth, recorded in both Ridgway's 1912 standard and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955.

sections.title: Earth, not flower
sections.body:
Our library records Clay pink from the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 and from Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, where it is grouped with his other clay-family names [1][2]. The ISCC-NBS block for this swatch is grayish reddish orange, only 3.0 units from that block's centroid [2]. It is a family-word variant built on [[clay]] itself, in our data's naming tree, rather than a separate coinage [2].

The name points to the color of fired or wet clay earth, not to a flower or fruit, which puts it among the mineral and landscape words in Ridgway's system alongside names like [[ochre]], [[terracotta]] and [[adobe]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Clay pink covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 326 of them, about 1.4 per cent, as photographed [3]. It is strikingly concentrated outside Europe: 80 of 721 Indian paintings, 5 of 25 Nepali paintings and 5 of 47 Tibetan paintings carry it, each several times the archive's overall rate [3]. Pontormo is its most devoted single painter here, in 3 of his 13 works [3]. As always, these are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen color, not a pigment test [3].
